# GEO report: harbor-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 68/100, Needs work

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 17 ÷ 25 × 100 = 68. High = (17 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 68.

Everything could be settled from the code. The score is held back by four things: two AI search crawlers are blocked, a default setting stops pages being quoted, every page's canonical points at the home page, and both pieces of structured data are broken. No quoted blocker caps the score at 40. The crawler block is the closest, but no policy is declared, so I assumed you want to be found.

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Stop blocking two AI search crawlers (GEO-009)
- **Why it matters:** `OAI-SearchBot` (ChatGPT search) and `PerplexityBot` are told to stay out of the whole site, so those tools can't read it.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4-8`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Disallow: /` and `User-agent: PerplexityBot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 80/100 (20 ÷ 25). If the block is deliberate, leave it and add `policy.aiSearchCrawlers` to `geo.config.json` to say so.

### 2. Fix the broken structured data (GEO-004)
- **Why it matters:** Structured data (JSON-LD) is a machine-readable label for page facts. The FAQ's first question has no answer key, and the Article is invalid JSON, so tools may ignore both.
- **Where:** `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`
- **What the code says:** `" ": {` (it should be `"acceptedAnswer"`), and `"headline": "Moorings and prices", }` (a trailing comma).
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 76/100 (19 ÷ 25).

### 3. Remove the page-wide snippet block (GEO-017)
- **Why it matters:** `max-snippet:0` tells search and AI tools they may show no text from the page, which works against being quoted.
- **Where:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`
- **What the code says:** `<meta name="robots" content={robots ?? "max-snippet:0"} />`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 76/100 (19 ÷ 25). Use `robots ?? "index, follow"`, or omit the tag when `robots` is unset.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines, tiny |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers can get in | Problem | `public/robots.txt:4-8`, 2 crawlers blocked site-wide (assumed goal: be found) |
| GEO-014 | Listed routes are indexable | Clear | `/` and `/moorings` are indexable. `/contact` is deliberately noindex (`contact.astro:4`) and not counted |
| GEO-015 | Canonical is absolute and correct | Problem | `Base.astro:8`, the same home URL on every page. `/` is right, `/moorings` is wrong (1 of 2 routes). Earns 1 of 2 |
| GEO-003 | Content is in server HTML | Clear | Astro static pages render on the server |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Problem | `faq.json:8`, `moorings.astro:9`. 0 of 2 routes |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is discoverable | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml` plus the `Sitemap:` line in `robots.txt:10` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and lang | Clear | `Base.astro:4-7`, all 3 pages set both |
| GEO-016 | Routes are linked with real links | Clear | `Base.astro:12`, `<a href>` navigation |
| GEO-017 | No snippet block | Problem | `Base.astro:9`. `/` and `/moorings` affected, 0 of 2 |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read `Newsletter.jsx` (wrapped label, text button) and `Base.astro`. No images in the code |
| GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | No mobile app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not scored | None present |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not scored | None present |

## Other problems found

- **A noindex page is in the sitemap.** `public/sitemap.xml:5` has `<url><loc>https://harbor.example/contact</loc></url>`, but `src/pages/contact.astro:4` sets `robots="noindex"`. Remove it from the sitemap.
- **`/moorings` points its canonical at the home page.** `src/layouts/Base.astro:8` has `<link rel="canonical" href="https://harbor.example/" />`. Pass a `canonical` prop, or build it from `new URL(Astro.url.pathname, Astro.site)`. This is the GEO-015 problem above.

## Worth considering

- **Show the FAQ on the page:** `src/pages/index.astro:8`: `<script type="application/ld+json" set:html={JSON.stringify(faq)}>`. The night-booking and water-taxi answers exist only inside the script. Render them as visible text too.
- **Deliver the mooring details the page promises:** `src/pages/moorings.astro:5`: `description="Mooring sizes and seasonal prices."`. The page gives only "Prices start at £40 a night." Add a table of sizes and seasonal prices.
- **Set `site` in the Astro config:** there is no `astro.config.*`, and the origin is hardcoded in `Base.astro:8`. Setting `site` lets you build canonicals and a generated sitemap from one value.
- **Add head basics:** `Base.astro:5-10` has no `charset` or `viewport` meta, and the body has no `<main>`. Add all three.
- **Link onward from the home page:** `index.astro:6-7` has two lines of text and no links beyond the nav. Link to the moorings and prices page from the text.
- **Name the site in machine-readable form:** nothing states the harbour's identity. Add `Organization` or `LocalBusiness` JSON-LD on the home page (name, location, phone `01326 000000`). It is already visible on `/contact`, which is deliberately noindex.
- **Make the home title match the page:** `index.astro:5` says "Harbor moorings in Cornwall" while the h1 says "Moorings in Falmouth". Naming Falmouth in the title would make it clearer.
- **Add `<lastmod>` to the sitemap entries** (`public/sitemap.xml:3-5`) once you have real dates.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live status codes and headers:** whether `/robots.txt` and the listed URLs answer 200, and whether the host adds an `X-Robots-Tag`, need a live check.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site, because there is no `geo.config.json` and so no declared policy.
- `harbor.example` is a placeholder domain. Replace it with your real one everywhere before launch.
- I read all 9 tracked files: `package.json`, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, the layout, 3 pages, the Newsletter component and `faq.json`. They give 3 routes and 2 JSON-LD sources.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
